title: Major US banks are blocking agents that log in with customer credentials
friendlyTitle: Big US banks are blocking agents that use your bank password
summary: The Decoder reports, citing Axios, that major US banks are restricting external AI agents that reach accounts with customer-provided usernames and passwords. It names Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo, and says Morgan Stanley already blocks agents entirely, with JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi moving the same way. That use breaks bank rules that require the account holder to log in personally. Morgan Stanley told reporters it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms. Most banks, The Decoder says, want agents limited to read-only access, and many cannot yet tell a user-directed agent from one acting on its own.
friendlySummary: The Decoder reports, citing Axios, that major US banks are restricting outside AI agents that get into accounts with a customer's own username and password. It names Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo. Morgan Stanley already blocks agents entirely. JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi are moving the same way. That use breaks bank rules that say the account holder must log in themselves. Morgan Stanley told reporters it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms. Most banks, The Decoder says, want agents limited to looking, not acting. Many still cannot tell an agent you sent from one acting on its own.
whyItMatters: Do not give a bank password to an agent, even one that asks nicely and offers to check a balance. The bank can treat that login as a breach of its terms, and it may not be able to undo a transfer the agent starts. A read-only connection, if your bank offers one, is the path that is actually being discussed. A pasted password is not.
